newsitem.title: USA: Jordan to divest most shares by end 1997-official.
newsitem.headline: Jordan to divest most shares by end 1997-official.

text.p: The government of Jordan plans to privatize most of its shares in cement, potash and oil companies, an Jordanian official said Monday.
"We are going to sell most of our equity in major blue chip companies," Jawad al-Anani, Jordan's deputy prime minister for development, told reporters here.
Anani said the government would sell 33 percent of state-owned outstanding equity in cement enterprises, as well as most of its shares in a potash company and oil refineries by the end of 1997.
"Jordan is fully committed to privatization," he said. "We're opening up our economy to the rest of the world."
Jordan would select a strategic partner for 26 percent of the state telecommunications firm within three months, and would privatize the electrical company by year-end, he said.

He said that Jordan's inaugural $70 million Eurobond announced last month would be issued in two-three months and would have a three year duration. The government might increase the size if it finds sufficient investor interest.
In addition, the government planned to issue $70 million in Treasury bills denominated in Jordanian dinars, the first of its kind, by September.
The minister was part a Citicorp-sponsored Jordan delegation that met with U.S. investment bankers here.
